- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., 2022-12-20 to 2023-01-11).
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias, particularly when recent history includes high values (e.g., 87+), suggesting model fails to account for mean reversion or volatility decay.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 89.30, 93.00, 95.60), model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward, indicating lag or overconfidence in momentum.
- Forecasts tend to be flat or slightly increasing, even when true outcomes show volatility or sharp declines (e.g., 89.30 → 82.94, 89.30 → 87.70).
- Model underestimates true price drops after high peaks (e.g., 89.30 → 82.94, 89.30 → 87.70).
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1-3 days) and fail to adjust for sudden market corrections.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts rise with recent history, even when true outcomes show downward drift.
- Forecasts are not sensitive to true outcome volatility — e.g., when true prices drop sharply (e.g., 89.30 → 82.94), model remains flat or slightly rising.
- Model fails to capture “rebound after correction” — e.g., after 82.94 → 87.70, model doesn’t adjust upward.
- Forecasts are not calibrated to true price range — e.g., when true prices are clustered around 80–90, model forecasts are consistently above 85–90.
- Model shows “false momentum” — forecasts rise with recent history even when true outcomes show no trend or reversal.
- Model underestimates true price volatility — e.g., when true prices swing from 89.30 to 82.94, model forecasts remain flat or slightly rising.
- Model fails to adjust for “reversal after spike” — e.g., after 89.30 → 82.94, model forecasts remain flat or slightly rising.
